slides.heading: Choosing the Right List Method
slides.body: Choosing the Right List Method is part of List Operations and Methods. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Choosing the Right List Method
slides.body: Choosing the right list method depends on the goal: add by position, add at the end, remove by value, remove by index, sort, or reverse.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Choosing a list method is like choosing the right tool: scissors, tape, or a stapler depending on the task.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Choose a list method based on the action you need: add, remove, reorder, check, slice, or copy.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Use the correct methods to add a task and then remove the last task.
slides.hint: Use append() to add and pop() to remove the last item.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Create a list, append Done, remove Done, and print the final list.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
